# Squares of a Sorted Array

## Problem

Implement `sortedSquares(nums)`. The input `nums` is an integer array whose values are arranged in non-decreasing order. Square every element and return the resulting values as a new array, also arranged in non-decreasing order.

Your solution is expected to run in linear time; squaring everything and then sorting the squares is not the intended approach.

Example 1:

```text
Input: nums = [-4,-1,0,3,10]

Output: [0,1,9,16,100]
```

Explanation: Squaring each entry yields `[16,1,0,9,100]`, and putting those values in order gives `[0,1,9,16,100]`.



Example 2:

```text
Input: nums = [-7,-3,2,3,11]

Output: [4,9,9,49,121]
```

Constraints:

* $$1 \le \text{nums.length} \le 10^4$$
* $$-10^4 \le \text{nums}[i] \le 10^4$$
* `nums` is in non-decreasing order.
* The algorithm must run in linear time, without sorting the squared values afterward.

## Follow-ups

* Can you solve the problem using constant extra space (not counting the output array)?

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

The input is sorted, so the largest squares can only come from the two ends of the array, because negatives with big magnitude square to big values.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use two pointers at the left and right ends and fill the output array from the back by repeatedly taking the larger absolute value.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

This gives O(n) time with O(n) output space, and you should check all-negative, all-positive and single-element inputs.

</details>
